Feature Importance TreeSHAP Permutation
Increases score Decreases score (SHAP)
TreeSHAP (left): mean |SHAP value| per feature — exact Shapley values from the tree structure. Order-independent and handles interactions.  Permutation (right): drop in AUC when a feature is randomly shuffled — model-agnostic and measures true predictive contribution.
TreeSHAP — mean |SHAP value|
Permutation — AUC drop
Partial Dependence (PDP) & Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE) all features
PDP: average model response as each feature sweeps its range (all other features marginalised). Bold line = population average.  ICE: one line per sampled instance — reveals heterogeneity hidden by the PDP average. Orange dashed = reference observation value.

Feature Interactions H-stat ⓘ Friedman H-statistic
Measures the fraction of the joint partial dependence variance of two features that is attributable to their interaction (not their individual effects). H=0 means no interaction; H≈1 means the joint effect is almost entirely interaction-driven.

Friedman & Popescu, 2008 — "Predictive Learning via Rule Ensembles"
Higher H = stronger non-additive interaction between the two features.

Known Limitations & Caveats
Velocity features assume single-account ownership
Joint or family accounts share velocity budget, increasing FP rate for shared cardholders.
Geo anomaly degrades for frequent international travelers
Customers with > 4 distinct country codes in 90 days show 2.3× higher FP rate.
Merchant risk score lags new merchant onboarding by 48–72h
Newly-onboarded legitimate merchants temporarily carry elevated risk scores.

Endpoints & Schemas

POST/v1/predict

Score a single transaction in real-time. Returns fraud probability, binary decision, and rule triggers.

P50: 12msP99: 47msSLO: 100ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "amount": 247.50,
 "merchant_id": "M8821",
 "account_id": "A44291",
 "timestamp": "2026-03-24T14:22:01Z"}
Response
{"score": 0.847,
 "decision": "REVIEW",
 "threshold": 0.70,
 "model_version": "run-009",
 "latency_ms": 14}
POST/v1/explain

Return SHAP feature attributions, human-readable narrative, and full rule evaluation trace — which rules were evaluated, which fired, and which set the final outcome.

P50: 38msP99: 142msSLO: 250ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "include_narrative": true,
 "include_rules": true,
 "top_k": 5}
Response
{"score": 0.847,
 "shap_values": {"txn_velocity_1h": 0.31,
   "merchant_risk_score": 0.24, ...},
 "base_value": 0.142,
 "top_drivers": ["txn_velocity_1h",
   "merchant_risk_score"],
 "narrative": "High velocity (9 txn/hr)...",
 "rule_trace": {
   "rules_evaluated": 6,
   "rules_fired": [
     {"id": "rule-4", "name": "Moderate review",
      "condition": "score >= 0.55 AND score < 0.80",
      "outcome": "REVIEW", "order": 4},
     {"id": "rule-5", "name": "High-risk block",
      "condition": "score >= 0.80 AND amount > 500",
      "outcome": "BLOCK", "order": 5}],
   "last_fired": "rule-5",
   "final_outcome": "BLOCK",
   "fallback_used": false
 }}
POST/v1/rules/evaluate

Evaluate the active rule set against a pre-scored record. Returns a complete rule-fire trace without re-invoking the ML model. Useful for auditing, appeals, and rule debugging.

P50: 4msP99: 11msSLO: 50ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "score": 0.847,
 "features": {
   "amount": 247.50,
   "merchant_category": "crypto",
   "velocity_24h": 9,
 "rule_set_version": "v14"}
Response
{"rule_set_version": "v14",
 "rules_evaluated": 6,
 "trace": [
   {"rule": "rule-1", "fired": false,
    "reason": "score 0.847 ≥ 0.40"},
   {"rule": "rule-4", "fired": true,
    "condition_met": "score in [0.55,0.80)",
    "outcome": "REVIEW"},
   {"rule": "rule-5", "fired": true,
    "condition_met": "score≥0.80 ∧ amt>500",
    "outcome": "BLOCK"}],
 "final_outcome": "BLOCK",
 "last_fired_rule": "rule-5",
 "fallback_used": false,
 "eval_ms": 3}

Rule Editor

Sequential engine · last-fired-wins
How it works: All rules are evaluated top-to-bottom on every prediction. Each rule that fires sets the outcome. The last rule to fire is the final decision. Drag rows to reorder. Rules with lower priority (higher number) override earlier ones.

Partial Dependence (PDP) & Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE) all features
PDP: average model response as each feature sweeps its range (all other features marginalised). Bold line = population average.  ICE: one line per sampled instance — reveals heterogeneity hidden by the PDP average. Orange dashed = reference observation value.

Feature Interactions H-stat ⓘ Friedman H-statistic
Measures the fraction of the joint partial dependence variance of two features that is attributable to their interaction (not their individual effects). H=0 means no interaction; H≈1 means the joint effect is almost entirely interaction-driven.

Friedman & Popescu, 2008 — "Predictive Learning via Rule Ensembles"
Higher H = stronger non-additive interaction between the two features.

What would change this decision?
No single-feature counterfactual would flip this decision — the risk signal is strong across multiple features.

Known Limitations & Caveats
DTI calculation uses stated income
Self-employed applicants with variable income may have understated or overstated DTI vs actual cash flow.
Payment history window is 24 months
Recent credit history (< 6 months) applicants are under-represented in training data; model may underestimate risk.
Income stability index uses employer payroll data
Gig/freelance income is not captured; affected applicants may appear more unstable than they are.

Endpoints & Schemas

POST/v1/predict

Score a single transaction in real-time. Returns fraud probability, binary decision, and rule triggers.

P50: 12msP99: 47msSLO: 100ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "amount": 247.50,
 "merchant_id": "M8821",
 "account_id": "A44291",
 "timestamp": "2026-03-24T14:22:01Z"}
Response
{"score": 0.847,
 "decision": "REVIEW",
 "threshold": 0.70,
 "model_version": "run-009",
 "latency_ms": 14}
POST/v1/explain

Return SHAP feature attributions, human-readable narrative, and full rule evaluation trace — which rules were evaluated, which fired, and which set the final outcome.

P50: 38msP99: 142msSLO: 250ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "include_narrative": true,
 "include_rules": true,
 "top_k": 5}
Response
{"score": 0.847,
 "shap_values": {"txn_velocity_1h": 0.31,
   "merchant_risk_score": 0.24, ...},
 "base_value": 0.142,
 "top_drivers": ["txn_velocity_1h",
   "merchant_risk_score"],
 "narrative": "High velocity (9 txn/hr)...",
 "rule_trace": {
   "rules_evaluated": 6,
   "rules_fired": [
     {"id": "rule-4", "name": "Moderate review",
      "condition": "score >= 0.55 AND score < 0.80",
      "outcome": "REVIEW", "order": 4},
     {"id": "rule-5", "name": "High-risk block",
      "condition": "score >= 0.80 AND amount > 500",
      "outcome": "BLOCK", "order": 5}],
   "last_fired": "rule-5",
   "final_outcome": "BLOCK",
   "fallback_used": false
 }}
POST/v1/rules/evaluate

Evaluate the active rule set against a pre-scored record. Returns a complete rule-fire trace without re-invoking the ML model. Useful for auditing, appeals, and rule debugging.

P50: 4msP99: 11msSLO: 50ms
Request
{"transaction_id": "txn_xyz",
 "score": 0.847,
 "features": {
   "amount": 247.50,
   "merchant_category": "crypto",
   "velocity_24h": 9,
 "rule_set_version": "v14"}
Response
{"rule_set_version": "v14",
 "rules_evaluated": 6,
 "trace": [
   {"rule": "rule-1", "fired": false,
    "reason": "score 0.847 ≥ 0.40"},
   {"rule": "rule-4", "fired": true,
    "condition_met": "score in [0.55,0.80)",
    "outcome": "REVIEW"},
   {"rule": "rule-5", "fired": true,
    "condition_met": "score≥0.80 ∧ amt>500",
    "outcome": "BLOCK"}],
 "final_outcome": "BLOCK",
 "last_fired_rule": "rule-5",
 "fallback_used": false,
 "eval_ms": 3}

Rule Editor

Sequential engine · last-fired-wins
How it works: All rules are evaluated top-to-bottom on every prediction. Each rule that fires sets the outcome. The last rule to fire is the final decision. Drag rows to reorder. Rules with lower priority (higher number) override earlier ones.

Project Description

Predicts the 30-day churn probability for retail banking customers. Output drives tiered retention interventions — HYSA promos, fee reversals, and relationship banker calls — ranked by a downstream recommendation model. Target: customers with DDA activity in the prior 90 days.

Why 0.18? Threshold Selection Rationale
Mathematical optimum
t = 0.18 ≈ F1-maximising threshold on the holdout. F1 peaks here because the precision gain from raising the threshold no longer offsets the recall loss.
Business constraint
At t = 0.18, ~1,100 customers are flagged per month — within the retention team's outreach capacity. At t = 0.10, that number grows to >1,800 and drowns the team.
Cost-benefit floor
Break-even is p > $75 ÷ $1,200 = 6.25%. At t = 0.18, the actual churn rate is 37.6% — 6× above break-even. Every intervention is NPV-positive.
Note
After calibration, raw model scores shift slightly. The operational threshold is re-evaluated against the calibrated score distribution before each campaign run.

Reliability Diagram — Uncalibrated vs. Calibrated

The model systematically over-predicts churn probability (bars fall below the diagonal). Isotonic regression post-processing corrects this, bringing dots close to the perfect calibration line.

Calibration Method Comparison
Why Calibration Matters Here
Break-even threshold6.25%
Raw score at break-even~10.4% raw
Without calibration, the cost-benefit threshold math is wrong — you're comparing a distorted probability against a dollar figure. Calibrate first, then set thresholds.
SR 11-7 requirement: Calibration results must be documented and the fitted calibrator must be version-controlled alongside the model artifact.

Break-even logic: Send an offer only when P(churn) > offer_cost ÷ LTV = $75 ÷ $1,200 = 6.25%. Operational threshold set at 18% to balance precision with outreach capacity.
Precision & Recall vs. Threshold

F1 peaks near t=0.16 (F1=0.488). At t=0.18: Precision 37.6%, Recall 56.3%, F1 0.45. Moving the threshold right improves precision (fewer wasted offers) but misses more churners.

2. Conceptual Soundness

Churn is defined as DDA account closure or zero-balance dormancy (>60 days) within 30 days of observation. Label was reviewed for leakage: features computed as of T−1 day; label computed at T+30. Temporal split (train: Jan 2022–Jun 2024; test: Oct–Dec 2024) prevents look-ahead bias.

WeightedEnsemble L2 (CatBoost + XGBoost base learners) was chosen over logistic regression after documented evaluation across 5 runs. Gradient boosting was selected for its ability to capture non-linear interactions in behavioral features. Alternative approaches (logistic regression, neural MLP) were benchmarked and documented in the experiment runs log.

5. Known Limitations
⚠ Seasonality: Model trained on 3 years including COVID-era behavioral shifts. Performance may degrade during macro-economic stress events.
⚠ Product mix: Low signal for customers with only savings accounts (no DDA).
⚠ PSI trigger: Re-train required if monthly PSI > 0.20 on any top-5 feature.
⚠ Intervention feedback: Model does not account for selection bias in past retention campaigns — survivors may be systematically different.
